newsitem.title: ITALY: Britain's Princess Diana awarded medal in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Princess Diana awarded medal in Italy.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana, who has said she would like to be to be the "queen of people's hearts", received a gold medal in Italy on Sunday for her charity activities and health care work.

Diana, who finally divorced heir to the throne Prince Charles in August, received the award from the Italian-based Pio Manzu International Research Centre, of which former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev is chairman.

A message from Gorbachev apologising for his absence was read out at the meeting before the princess was given her medal. In her acceptance speech in the north-eastern seaside resort town of Rimini, Diana spoke about old age.
South African ambassador to Italy Conscet Ginvala received another award on behalf of President Nelson Mandela.

The visit to Italy was Diana's first overseas trip since Britain's tabloid Sun newspaper apologised after last week printing what it said were black and white photographs showing Diana cavorting with former lover James Hewitt.
The newspaper later admitted it had been hoaxed and that the video from which the pictures were taken was staged with lookalike actors as a pilot for a comedy show.
